title: Open Redirect in OAuth2 Filter via Unvalidated 'state' Parameter
analysis:
### Source
Untrusted input enters through the `state` query parameter in an HTTP request directed at the OAuth callback endpoint (e.g., `/_oauth`), parsed via `Http::Utility::QueryParamsMulti::parseQueryString(path_str)` in `OAuth2Filter::decodeHeaders`.

### Sanitization / Validation
The filter performs minimal parsing on `state` via `state_url.initialize(state, false)` and verifies `!config_->redirectPathMatcher().match(state_url.pathAndQueryParams())` to prevent infinite redirect loops back to the callback path itself. However, the filter fails to perform any validation on the destination authority/host: `state_url.hostAndPort()` is never compared against `host_` or validated against an allowed domains list, allowing arbitrary external domains.

### Sink
In `OAuth2Filter::decodeHeaders` (lines 349-353), the filter constructs a `302 Found` HTTP response setting the `Location` header directly to the unvalidated `state` value (`{Http::Headers::get().Location, state}`) and calls `decoder_callbacks_->encodeHeaders(...)`. (A similar flow exists in `finishGetAccessTokenFlow` at line 619).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
An attacker lures an authenticated victim (or a victim in the process of authenticating) to access:
```http
GET /_oauth?state=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.example.com%2Fphishing HTTP/1.1
Host: secure-app.example.com
Cookie: OauthHMAC=<valid_session_hmac>
```
Because the victim has an active session, `canSkipOAuth(headers)` returns `true`, and the path matches `redirectPathMatcher()`. Envoy decodes `state` to `https://evil.example.com/phishing`, confirms it is a parseable URL whose path (`/phishing`) does not match `/_oauth`, and immediately responds with:
```http
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://evil.example.com/phishing
```
This forces the victim's browser to navigate to the attacker's site.
vuln_type: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
